analysis:
The PR changes one line in each of two test-only files. MTPResliceFallbackTests.swift line 81 (MTPFloorTarget) and ProviderMTPFactoryTests.swift line 28 (MTPFactoryTarget) move from `prepare(_:cache:windowSize:)` to `prepare(_:cache:state:prefill:)`. This tracks an upstream mlx-swift-lm LanguageModel protocol signature change. Both stubs still return `.tokens(input.text)` and neither touches production code.

The edits stay inside test fixtures. They do not alter encryption, attestation, authorization, the coordinator WebSocket contract, key handling or the SSD prefix cache (T-041 and related). Production sources are untouched and I did not verify them. The remaining integration question is whether the production LanguageModel conformances and the MLX dependency pin are updated in the same PR. That is a build and compatibility matter. It is not a security regression, and it is outside the supplied evidence.

The surrounding test content in MTPResliceFallbackTests.swift (fake HF snapshot written under the HF cache dir, temporary artifact directories) is pre-existing and unchanged. I identified no new attack surface.
